arxiv-2103-08960.title: On the Electromagnetic Response of Topological Superconductors
arxiv-2103-08960.creator: M. Stålhammar 1, M. Stone 2, Masatoshi Sato 3, T.H. Hansson 1
arxiv-2103-08960.description: Abstract We resolve several puzzles related to the electromagnetic response of topological superconductors in 3+1 dimensions. In particular we show by an analytical calculation that the interface between a topological and normal superconductor does not exhibit any quantum Hall effect as long as time reversal invariance is preserved.

arxiv-2106-00345.title: Decay of the vortex muon
arxiv-2106-00345.creator: Pengcheng Zhao, Igor P. Ivanov, Pengming Zhang
arxiv-2106-00345.description: Abstract Muon decay is self-analyzing: the spectral-angular distribution of the emitted electron reveals the spin orientation of the polarized muon. Here, we show that the same feature applies to muons in non-plane-wave states and helps reveal the rich polarization opportunities available.

arxiv-2201-03065.title: Selecting the Best Optimizing System We gratefully acknowledge helpful discussions with Steve Chick, Weiwei Fan, Shane Henderson, Jeff Hong, Peter Glynn, Guanghui Lan, and Barry Nelson. All errors are ours.
arxiv-2201-03065.creator: Nian Si, Zeyu Zheng
arxiv-2201-03065.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nian Si, Zeyu Zheng. We formulate selecting the best optimizing system (SBOS) problems and provide solutions for those problems. In an SBOS problem, a finite number of systems are contenders. Inside each system, a continuous decision variable affects the system’s expected performance. An SBOS problem compares different systems based on their expected performances under their own optimally chosen decision to select the best, without advance knowledge of expected performances of the systems nor the optimizing decision inside each system.

arxiv-2310-17481.title: Intermediate Field Coupling of Single Epitaxial Quantum Dots to Plasmonic Waveguides
arxiv-2310-17481.creator: Michael Seidel, Yuhui Yang, Thorsten Schumacher, Yongheng Huo, Saimon Filipe Covre da Silva, Sven Rodt, Armando Rastelli, Stephan Reitzenstein, Markus Lippitz
arxiv-2310-17481.description: Abstract Key requirements for quantum plasmonic nanocircuits are reliable single-photon sources, high coupling efficiency to the plasmonic structures and low propagation losses. Self-assembled epitaxially grown GaAs quantum dots are close to ideal stable, bright and narrowband single-photon emitters. Likewise, wet-chemically grown monocrystalline silver nanowires are among the best plasmonic waveguides.

arxiv-2312-04252.title: A Mott-Schottky Analysis of Mesoporous Silicon in Aqueous Electrolyte by Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
arxiv-2312-04252.creator: Manuel Brinker, Patrick Huber
arxiv-2312-04252.description: Abstract Nanoporosity in silicon leads to completely new functionalities of this mainstream semiconductor. In recent years, it has been shown that filling the pores with aqueous electrolytes in addition opens a particularly wide field for modifying and achieving active control of these functionalities, e.g., for electrochemo-mechanical actuation and tunable photonics, or for the design of on-chip supercapacitors.

arxiv-2312-11823.title: Singular Control of (Reflected) Brownian Motion: A Computational Method Suitable for Queueing Applications
arxiv-2312-11823.creator: Baris Ata, J. Michael Harrison, Nian Si
arxiv-2312-11823.description: Abstract Motivated by applications in queueing theory, we consider a class of singular stochastic control problems whose state space is the d d -dimensional positive orthant. The original problem is approximated by a drift control problem, to which we apply a recently developed computational method that is feasible for dimensions up to d = 30 d=30 or more.

arxiv-2403-12823.title: Multi-Shot Answer Set Programming for Flexible Payroll Management
arxiv-2403-12823.creator: BENJAMIN CALLEWAERT, JOOST VENNEKENS
arxiv-2403-12823.description: Abstract Payroll management is a critical business task that is subject to a large number of rules, which vary widely between companies, sectors, and countries. Moreover, the rules are often complex and change regularly. Therefore, payroll management systems must be flexible in design.

arxiv-2503-07693.title: Fully Autonomous Programming using Iterative Multi-Agent Debugging with Large Language Models
arxiv-2503-07693.creator: Anastasiia Grishina, Vadim Liventsev, Aki Härmä, Leon Moonen
arxiv-2503-07693.description: Abstract . Program synthesis with Large Language Models (LLMs) suffers from a “near-miss syndrome”: the generated code closely resembles a correct solution but fails unit tests due to minor errors. We address this with a multi-agent framework called Synthesize, Execute, Instruct, Debug, and Repair (SEIDR).

arxiv-2508-19110.title: Exact Persistent Stochastic Non-Interference
arxiv-2508-19110.creator: Carla Piazza, Riccardo Romanello, Sabina Rossi
arxiv-2508-19110.description: Abstract Persistent Stochastic Non-Interference (PSNI) was introduced to capture a quantitative security property in stochastic process algebras, ensuring that a high-level process does not influence the observable behaviour of a low-level component, as formalised via lumpable bisimulation. In this work, we revisit PSNI from a performance-oriented perspective and propose a new characterisation based on a refined behavioural relation.

arxiv-2512-03655.title: V-Reactor Dynamics: Dual Chaotic System and Rewriting the Antiviral Response History
arxiv-2512-03655.creator: Yong-Shou Chen
arxiv-2512-03655.description: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic revealed a key vulnerability: our failure to anticipate novel viral threats. Moving beyond descriptive virology, we introduce V-Reactor Dynamics (V-Dynamics), a physics-based framework modeling host-virus interaction as a synchronized dual chaotic system. This paradigm predicts viral evolution, immune response, transmission, and virulence through equations governed by the parameter reactivity ( \rho ).

pmc-10751305.title: A hematological parameter-based model for distinguishing non-puerperal mastitis from invasive ductal carcinoma
pmc-10751305.creator: Zhichun Wang, Lin Hua, Xiaofeng Liu, Xueli Chen, Guohui Xue
pmc-10751305.description: PurposeNon-puerperal mastitis (NPM) accounts for approximately 4-5% of all benign breast lesions. Ultrasound is the preferred method for screening breast diseases; however, similarities in imaging results can make it challenging to distinguish NPM from invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Our objective was to identify convenient and objective hematological markers to distinguish NPM from IDC.

pmc-12504527.title: Fate mapping of peripherally-derived macrophages after traumatic brain injury in mice reveals a long-lasting population with a distinct transcriptomic signature
pmc-12504527.creator: Maria Serena Paladini, Benjamin A Yang, Kristof A Torkenczy, Elma S Frias, Xi Feng, Karen Krukowski, Rene Sit, Maurizio Morri, Wendy Lam, Valentina Pedoia, Stefka Tyanova, Marco Colonna, Amber L Nolan, Susanna Rosi
pmc-12504527.description: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is an environmental risk factor for dementia and long-term neurological deficits, posing a significant public health challenge. TBI-induced neuroinflammation involves both brain-resident microglia and peripheral monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs). Previous research has shown that MDMs contribute to the development of long-term memory deficits, yet their long-term behavior following brain infiltration remains unclear.

pmc-12587283.title: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy diagnosis and management: a systematic review of clinical practice guidelines and recommendations with insights for future research
pmc-12587283.creator: Lorena Iezzi, Anna Sorella, Kristian Galanti, Sabina Gallina, Anwar A Chahal, Barbara Bauce, Alberto Cipriani, Rui Providencia, Luis R Lopes, Fabrizio Ricci, Mohammed Y Khanji
pmc-12587283.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is addressed in international guidelines and expert consensus statements. To assist clinicians in their routine practice and support decision-making, we performed a systematic review of the most relevant guidelines and recommendations for ACM diagnosis and management.

pmc-13399016.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of AI Consent Forms in Otolaryngologic Surgery
pmc-13399016.creator: Sholem Hack, Rebecca Attal, Armin Farzad, Lilia Ann Crew, Shmuel Silverstein, Jacob E Karni, Nir Livneh, Shibli Alsleibi, Naseem Saleh, Ben Gvili, David Yogev, Eric Remer, Eran E Alon, Gil Siegal, Masayoshi Takashima, Habib G Zalzal
pmc-13399016.description: IntroductionSurgical consent documents are frequently written at reading levels exceeding average health literacy. Large language models (LLMs) may offer a scalable approach to generating clearer, procedure‐specific consent forms. uslaw-usc-t12-s4528.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s4528.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 46 (Government Sponsored Enterprises); Subchapter I (Supervision And Regulation Of Enterprises); Part A (Financial Safety And Soundness Regulator). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. All public data assets published by the Agency shall be— (1) made available as an open Government data asset (as defined in section 3502 of title 44); (2) freely available.
